content: This medication should be used exactly as prescribed by your doctor, typically administered twice daily, approximately every 12 hours. If you are instructed to use more than one spray at a time, ensure you wait 30 seconds between each spray. Avoid spraying this medication into your eyes. Additionally, refrain from sneezing during or immediately after using this medication, as this may reduce the amount of medication absorbed. Follow the detailed instructions provided for cleaning the spray tip. It is crucial to continue using this medication exactly as directed by your doctor without skipping any doses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist to determine how long each bottle of the nasal spray should last. Do not use the nasal spray bottle beyond the recommended duration, even if there is medication remaining, as you may not receive a full dose. Do not increase your dose or use this medication more frequently or for a longer duration than prescribed. When starting this medication, you may experience a temporary worsening of symptoms. For women treating endometriosis, this could include increased vaginal bleeding. For children treating early puberty, symptoms may include vaginal bleeding, increased breast size, pubic hair growth, oily skin, or body odor. These symptoms typically improve after the first month of treatment. Common side effects in children may include nasal irritation, hot flashes, or vaginal discharge. In women, side effects may include nasal irritation, hot flashes, headaches, decreased sexual interest, muscle pain, vaginal dryness, acne, or a decrease in breast size. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. However, children using nafarelin may be at risk for increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension). Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. Before using nafarelin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to GnRH or other GnRH-like hormones (e.g., leuprolide), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. Women should begin this medication between days 2 and 4 of their menstrual cycle. While periods and ovulation may stop during treatment, this is not a reliable form of birth control. Discuss the use of non-hormonal birth control methods (e.g., condoms, diaphragms with spermicide) with your doctor. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication due to potential risks to the infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., tests for pituitary gonadotropic and gonadal functions), potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab and/or medical tests (e.g., growth or bone age velocity in children) should be conducted while using this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the bottle upright at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze. Avoid storing this medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
